issues.description: EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED membership check uses a list where a set or tuple fits better
issues.detail: The `_enable_vad` check builds a Python list literal for an `in` test on every init. A tuple (or a module-level frozenset) is the right data structure for a fixed membership test: cheaper, communicates immutability, and matches the shape of the data (a small, fixed set of sentinel enum values). Small thing, but data shape should match intent.

issues.description: Default turn_detection_mode flip is a silent behavior change for existing callers
issues.detail: Changing the default from EXTERNAL to FIXED alters runtime behavior for every existing user who relied on the default. The data structure (the enum) didn't change, but the meaning of "unspecified" did. At minimum the changelog should be in `.changed.md` not `.fixed.md`, and the docstring should call out the migration. Defaults are an API surface.

issues.description: split_sentences plumbed as Optional[bool] then coerced with `or False`
issues.detail: `split_sentences: bool | None = None` followed by `params.split_sentences or False` is the wrong data shape. If the value is a bool with a default of False, declare it `bool = False` and pass it through. The tri-state (None/True/False) buys nothing here and forces a coercion at the use site. Pick the shape, drop the dance.

issues.description: Commented-out `start_processing_metrics` line was moved, not deleted
issues.detail: The diff relocates `# await self.start_processing_metrics()` from after the broadcast to before it. Commented code is dead data; if it's needed later, git remembers. Either uncomment it (and explain ordering) or delete it. Carrying it forward in a new position implies intent that isn't documented.

issues.description: Warning branch on VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame when internal VAD is enabled is unreachable in practice
issues.detail: `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame` is emitted by Pipecat's VAD pipeline. If `_enable_vad` is True the service is delegating to the engine's VAD, so receiving this frame at all suggests upstream misconfiguration. The warn-and-do-nothing branch is fine, but consider whether the simpler shape is: subscribe to the frame only when `not self._enable_vad`, and drop the conditional entirely.

review.summary: Small, targeted patch. The data structures are mostly fine, but two shape mismatches stand out: a tri-state Optional[bool] for what is really a boolean flag, and a list literal used for a fixed membership test. The default-value flip from EXTERNAL to FIXED is the real risk here — that's an API change dressed as a fix, and the changelog filename understates it. Cleverness audit is clean; no fancy algorithms, no premature abstraction. Strip the Optional, tuple the membership check, and re-label the changelog.
